item.title: Fed’s Warsh Lays Out Data Dashboard to Read US Economy
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh used his keynote speech in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, last week to map out some of the key data points he leans on to read the US economy, offering new insight into his approach to policy making.

item.title: EU Moves to Support Ukraine Grain Exports and Shield Farmers
item.description: The European Union is looking “at all possible lanes” to support grain exports from Ukraine and is working to blunt the financial impact of extreme weather on farmers as part of a responsibility to safeguard global food supply, according to the bloc’s agriculture commissioner.

item.title: Nvidia’s Huang Urges G20 to Speed AI Adoption as Key to Growth
item.description: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang called on Group of 20 nations to accelerate their adoption of artificial intelligence as a way to enhance growth, urging the world’s largest economies to expand data centers and other infrastructure to support the emerging technology.

item.title: ElevenLabs Hires OpenAI VP as First Chief Revenue Officer
item.description: ElevenLabs has hired former OpenAI executive Ashley Kramer as its first chief revenue officer, part of the startup’s efforts to drum up business demand for its artificial intelligence voice tools.

item.title: Fed’s Williams Says Inflation Continuing to Trend Down
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said there’s evidence inflation continues to ease as the impact of tariffs fades while higher energy prices are not spreading to other services.

item.title: India Raises Record $127 Billion in Forex Deposits From Diaspora
item.description: India garnered a record of about $127 billion in foreign-currency inflows from its 35-million-strong diaspora since June through a special dollar-swap window, giving policymakers a bigger cushion to support the rupee if external pressures intensify.

item.title: Boehringer Signs Deal for Owkin AI, Joining Astra and Sanofi
item.description: Boehringer Ingelheim GmbH agreed to use Owkin’s artificial-intelligence model to help discover new oncology and immunology medicines.

item.title: College M&A Tool Helps Schools Connect in Grim Higher Ed Era
item.description: A new tool is trying to connect colleges with potential partners as higher education institutions face a shrinking pipeline of students.

item.title: OpenAI Faces New Lawsuits Linked to Shooting at Canadian School
item.description: OpenAI was hit with multiple lawsuits claiming the artificial intelligence company could have prevented a mass shooting in Canada earlier this year by informing law enforcement about the suspected killer’s messages with the popular chatbot ChatGPT.

item.title: Norwegian Hydro Stocks Hit Record Low, Raising Power Price Risks
item.description: Reservoirs that supply southern Norway with electricity fell to a record low for this time of year, raising the risk of higher power prices and greater reliance on natural gas across Europe this winter.

item.title: India’s Zerodha Gets Merchant Banking Permit as IPO Market Booms
item.description: A unit of Zerodha Broking Ltd., India’s second-largest broker founded by billionaire Nithin Kamath, secured a merchant banking license as the nation’s booming equity capital market draws new entrants seeking a share of record fees.

item.title: Deutsche Telekom Names New CFO, CTO in Management Reshuffle
item.description: Deutsche Telekom AG has named Dhananjay Mirchandani as its next chief financial officer, part of a number of executive changes at the top of Europe’s biggest telecommunications company.

item.title: Dutch Central Bank Shifts Gold From US on ‘Geopolitical Unrest’
item.description: The Dutch Central Bank has shifted more than a quarter of its gold reserves held in the US and Canada to the UK, citing concerns about geopolitical unrest.

item.title: US Companies Added 38,000 Jobs in August, ADP Data Show
item.description: US companies added jobs at a more moderate pace in August, underscoring a stable labor market.

item.title: Venezuela’s New Crop of Oil Barons Step Up the Dealmaking
item.description: The country’s next generation of tycoons looks very different to what came before.

item.title: Wren House Is Said to Near Deal for GIC’s Data Center Stake
item.description: Wren House Infrastructure Management is nearing a deal to buy GIC Pte’s stake in a European data center joint venture, people with knowledge of the matter said.

item.title: Tencent-Backed Enflame’s IPO Draws 4,073 Times Retail Demand
item.description: The initial public offering of Shanghai Enflame Technology Co., a company backed by Tencent Holdings Ltd., drew strong demand from retail investors, as the last of the so-called “four little dragons” of leading Chinese artificial intelligence chipmakers taps the public market.

item.title: Apollo’s Slok Says US Yields Set to Rise on Iran War, Tariffs
item.description: US yields are likely to head higher driven by the Iran war and tariffs, but the upward pressure has little to do with the fiscal situation, according to Apollo Global Management Chief Economist Torsten Slok.

item.title: Uber to Cut 3,300 Jobs in Company Overhaul to Reduce Management Layers
item.description: Uber Technologies Inc. is cutting about 3,300 roles, or 10% of its staff globally, in a massive restructuring aimed at reducing management layers and reallocating spending into its ride-sharing, delivery and robotaxi businesses.

item.title: Micron, SK Hynix Provide Surprise Twist to US Chips Acts Debate
item.description: The memory-chip makers were a low priority when the US sought to revive domestic manufacturing

item.title: G20 Examines Debt Distress in Others, While Ignoring Own Challenges
item.description: Finance chiefs focused on developing nations’ debt while sidestepping their own borrowing

item.title: Oura Taps Netflix, Robinhood Veterans for Board Ahead of IPO
item.description: Oura, the maker of popular smart rings that track health, fitness, and sleep, is expanding its board of directors as it prepares for an initial public offering.The company said Wednesday that it is appointing four new independent directors with public company experience. item.title: Logistics Costs and Inflation Concerns
item.description: Transport, inventory and warehousing costs show few signs of easing

item.title: SNB Bank Council Leadership Will Change With Ammann Appointed
item.description: Switzerland’s government appointed Christoph Ammann as the next president of the Swiss National Bank’s Bank Council, the panel that oversees the institution.

item.title: Brazil Election: Lula Adviser Shuns Austerity as Investors Seek Spending Cuts
item.description: Brazil President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s policy platform chief pushed back against investor proposals to cut public spending, saying in an interview that austerity would be unnecessary if the leftist wins reelection.

item.title: AI Layoffs at Microsoft, Amazon, Meta Drive Seattle Luxury Home Sales Down 15%
item.description: Job cuts in the Seattle area are hurting luxury real estate sales

item.title: Ghana Inflation Resumes Upswing, Supports Case for Rate Hold
item.description: Ghana’s annual inflation rate resumed its upswing in August as the rise in oil prices caused by the war in Iran seeped into transport and utility costs.

item.title: AI Fund Chief Urges UK Government to Think Like an Investor to Boost Startups
item.description: The head of the UK’s £500 million ($675 million) Sovereign AI Fund urged the government to adopt an investor mindset as ministers seek to spur growth in the domestic industry.

item.title: South Africa Business Mood Stuck at Level Too Low for Investment
item.description: South African business sentiment dropped to a two-year low in the third quarter, reflecting elevated uncertainty as conflict in the Middle East rages on and domestic demand falters.

item.title: Brazil’s Global Beef Dominance Collides With Tougher EU Rule
item.description: Brazil’s global dominance in the beef trade is clashing with tougher European standards, threatening exports as suppliers struggle to certify cattle under new restrictions on growth-promoting drugs.
